traps.reason: redactConfig passes buffers through without redaction. That looks like a leak, but it is deliberate: binary payloads cannot carry the string keys being redacted, and copying them would be wasteful. It is a redaction guard, not a defect.

The rewrite guard looks inverted, but it implements the documented AxiosHeaders.set contract: rewrite=true always overwrites, rewrite=false never overwrites an existing non-false value, and undefined only overwrites when the current value is not the literal false.
Dividing by freq looks unsafe, but the throttled wrapper is only constructed with a validated positive frequency and the caller owns that contract. There is no zero-division path from this module.
Dropping duplicate headers from a fixed list is required by the HTTP spec (node ignores duplicates of these fields), not a bug. Headers outside the list are concatenated with ', '.
Reverse iteration looks risky, but it is deliberate: listeners may unsubscribe themselves while the list is being notified, and iterating backwards keeps the remaining indexes valid.

expected.statement: isAbsoluteURL treats any non-string input as an absolute URL: a missing or non-string url bypasses the scheme check and is returned as absolute instead of false.
combineURLs concatenates the base and the relative URL without the separator, so a relative path is glued to the last path segment of the base URL.
buildURL keeps the hash mark when stripping the fragment, so serialized params are appended after the fragment and never reach the server.
InterceptorManager.forEach no longer skips null slots, so it calls the iteration callback with null for every ejected interceptor.
start() assigns a new interval without clearing the existing timer, so calling start() twice leaks the first interval and it keeps firing.
store.save is not awaited before store.get, so the read can return the previous token instead of the value that was just saved.
header names are no longer lower-cased during parsing, so Content-Type and content-type become distinct keys and a lookup by the canonical lower-case name returns undefined.
a response status below 500 is resolved before validateStatus decides, so 4xx client errors are delivered as successful responses and the caller's rejection handler never runs.
any object that does not explicitly set isAxiosError to false is classified as an AxiosError, so errors from other libraries are reported as axios errors with undefined response and config.
the trailing invocation uses the arguments of the call that scheduled the timer instead of the most recent call, so the latest payload is dropped when calls are throttled.
the cancellation request returns early while no reason exists yet, so the first cancel() call is silently ignored and the request is never cancelled.
spread passes the whole array as a single argument instead of expanding it, so a wrapped callback receives one array where the original call passed N positional arguments.
buildURL ignores a caller-supplied encode function and always uses the default encoder, so custom parameter encoding passed through options is silently dropped.
a FormData field name ending in [] is stored under the literal key [] instead of pushing onto an array, so repeated array fields collapse into one literal property.
cookies are split on the two-character separator "; " only, but browsers may serialize cookie pairs without the space, so a cookie that follows a space-less separator is not found.
transformData stops passing the response status to response transformers, so a transformer that branches on the status (for example parses JSON only for 2xx) can no longer see it.
